items.text: TRUMP PROMISES $5,000 DIVIDEND IF GOP WINS MIDTERMS President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 payment to every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans retain control of Congress in November. Trump credited U.S. economic performance for the proposal, which would cost more than $1 trillion. He also urged supporters to “pretend that I’m on the ballot,” effectively framing the midterms as a referendum on his presidency. Trump said oil prices would fall once the war with Iran ends.

HOUTHIS SEIZE STRATEGIC RED SEA CITY Iran-backed Houthis have seized Yemen’s Mocha, according to Reuters sources. The advance brings the group closer to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, raising risks for Red Sea shipping and global trade.

HUAWEI HIKES AI CHIP PRICES 60% Huawei has reportedly raised the price of its Ascend 950DT AI accelerator by about 60% to $37,300, as booming demand outstrips supply. HBM shortages are adding to costs, while demand for Chinese alternatives to Nvidia continues to surge.

PUTIN AIDE: EUROPE DOES NOT WANT UKRAINE PEACE Putin aide Nikolay Patrushev claimed Western Europe is not interested in peace in Ukraine or encouraging Kyiv to negotiate. He said the U.S. appears more interested in negotiations, expressing hope Washington could push Kyiv toward talks.

META - JPMORGAN TURNS BULLISH ON META’S AI POTENTIAL JPMorgan upgraded Meta to Overweight and raised its price target to $820 from $640, implying roughly 24% upside. The bank sees significant new revenue opportunities from AI agents, subscriptions and enterprise AI services beyond advertising.

SPCX - UK DEEPENS SPACEX RELIANCE WITH $40 MILLION SATELLITE SPEND Britain has spent nearly $40 million on SpaceX satellite services, becoming the first country outside the U.S. to publicly acknowledge adopting Starshield. The UK military operates roughly 1,000 Starshield and 500 Starlink terminals, increasingly shifting operational communications to the military-focused Starshield network. US, IRAN PREPARE FOR PROTRACTED WAR Iran and the U.S. are reportedly preparing for a potentially prolonged conflict, with little sign of an imminent ceasefire or normalization of Middle East energy flows. Bloomberg reports Tehran remains committed to fighting and has rebuilt missile capabilities, while the WSJ says top White House advisers have warned Trump the war could potentially last through 2029. HOUTHIS CLOSE IN ON KEY RED SEA CHOKEPOINT Iran-aligned Houthis have seized Yemen’s port city of Mocha and are pushing toward Dhubab and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, according to Reuters sources. Control of the strategic waterway could allow the group to further disrupt global shipping and Saudi oil exports, particularly as Hormuz remains constrained. Brent crude remained above $100 as risks to both major Middle East energy routes intensify.

TRUMP TOUTS “SOLD OUT” GOP MIDTERM CONVENTION President Donald Trump claimed the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas drew record attendance and stronger overall viewership than the NFL. Trump said thousands were unable to enter the packed arena and announced he will return tonight to deliver the convention’s closing remarks.

AAPL - MORGAN STANLEY SEES “APPLE AI” BULL CASE STRENGTHENING Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring maintains Overweight with a $360 price target, saying Apple’s latest launches represent a major step-up in innovation. He sees the iPhone Duo as Apple’s most innovative device in years, while stronger iPhone 18 Pro upgrades and broader Apple Intelligence integration could accelerate replacements. ECB SAYS INTEREST RATES ECB DECIDED TO RAISE THREE INTEREST RATES BY 25 BASIS POINTS

ECB HIKES RATES 25 BPS AS INFLATION RISKS RISE The ECB raised rates by 25 basis points, taking the deposit rate to 2.50%, as the Middle East conflict keeps inflation pressures elevated. The ECB now sees inflation averaging 3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028, with the latter two forecasts revised higher. Growth forecasts were also upgraded, while the ECB stressed that future rate decisions remain data-dependent with no pre-set path.

WALL STREET SEES 5% TREASURY YIELD RISK A Reuters poll found 17 of 31 bond strategists see the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield potentially hitting 5% within three months. The 10-year recently reached 4.86%, pressured by $100+ oil, inflation concerns and heavy government borrowing. Strategists still forecast yields eventually falling, but conviction is weakening as Fed hike expectations and fiscal concerns rise.

TRUMP SITS DOWN FOR EXCLUSIVE INGRAHAM INTERVIEW President Donald Trump has given Laura Ingraham an exclusive interview, with Part One airing tonight at 7 PM ET on The Ingraham Angle. Fox’s current schedule confirms the program’s 7 PM ET slot.

PENTAGON REJECTS AI “DOOMSDAY” WARNINGS Pentagon tech chief Emil Michael pushed back on warnings that AI could destroy humanity, calling fears of mass job losses and runaway AI part of a growing “doom loop.” Meanwhile, the Pentagon has already shifted 90% of its classified AI workload away from Anthropic following a major dispute over military AI restrictions.

IRAN STRIKE DAMAGES U.S. WARPLANES IN JORDAN Iranian strikes on a U.S. base in Jordan damaged multiple American military aircraft, a U.S. official told Reuters. One A-10 lost a wing, while roughly eight F-15s sustained light damage and returned to service. The attack also forced U.S. forces to fire around 30 Patriot interceptors, adding pressure to already strained air-defense stockpiles.

U.S. DIESEL SURGES ABOVE $5 AS SUPPLY SQUEEZE DEEPENS U.S. diesel futures surged above $5 a gallon for the first time since 2022, as Middle East disruptions and Russia’s export ban tighten global supplies. Retail diesel has already hit a record $5.98 nationally, with California averaging $7.91. The surge threatens to raise transportation costs and fuel inflation, adding pressure on consumers and the Fed.

IRGC CLAIMS U.S. DRONE DESTROYED IN HORMUZ Iran’s IRGC Navy claims it destroyed a U.S. unmanned vessel at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, identifying it as hull number 5838. The IRGC also declared that Hormuz remains blocked and under Iranian control, warning that hostile vessels will be targeted. The claims have not been independently verified.

IRAN REBUILDING BALLISTIC MISSILE ARSENAL Iran has resumed production of ballistic missiles, using stockpiled components and underground facilities, according to U.S. and Middle Eastern officials cited by the WSJ. Despite heavy strikes on its missile infrastructure, Iran is reportedly assembling both liquid- and solid-propellant missiles, potentially restoring capabilities the U.S. and Israel had sought to degrade.

US CPI PREVIEW 🇺🇸 Friday’s August US CPI report could be one of the most consequential inflation prints in months, with the outcome potentially tipping the balance on whether the Fed hikes rates at next week’s FOMC meeting. Consensus expectations point to headline CPI rising around 0.4% MoM, a sharp acceleration from 0.1% in July, while core CPI is expected around 0.2% MoM. NVDA - NVIDIA’S HUANG SEES CYBERSECURITY AS AI’S NEXT BIG MARKET Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says cybersecurity will likely become AI’s next major use case, as AI-generated code accelerates both software development and vulnerabilities. Huang said rapidly evolving threats will drive greater demand for AI-powered security and automated defenses, creating another major growth market for the technology.

OPENAI: LAUNCHES CHATGPT FOR FINANCIAL SERVICES WITH GPT-6 ASTRA REASONING

OPENAI LAUNCHES CHATGPT FOR WALL STREET OpenAI is launching ChatGPT for Financial Services, targeting investment bankers and equity researchers with integrated data from LSEG, PitchBook and Daloopa. Powered initially by GPT-6 Astra, the platform is designed to build research, financial models and client materials while providing granular source citations. The move intensifies OpenAI’s competition with Anthropic for lucrative financial-sector enterprise clients.

MUNI YIELDS SURGE TO HIGHEST SINCE APRIL 2025 U.S. 10-year municipal bond yields jumped to 3.62%, the highest since April 2025, tracking the Treasury selloff. JPMorgan says rising Treasury yields, heavy muni issuance and weak reinvestment demand are pressuring the market. Investors pulled roughly $460 million from muni funds Wednesday, the largest outflow since April 2025.
BRENT CRUDE FUTURES RISE BY $7 A BARREL AS US-IRAN CONFLICT INTENSIFIES

U.S. CONTAINER IMPORTS HIT THIRD-HIGHEST LEVEL EVER U.S. container imports reached 2.6 million TEUs in August, the third-highest monthly level on record, according to Descartes. Volumes rose 3% year-over-year and 22% versus August 2019, signaling resilient consumer demand despite tariffs and inflation. Shipping costs remain elevated, with Shanghai-New York rates more than doubling from last year amid Red Sea and Hormuz disruptions.
BESSENT: GOING TO SANCTION A LARGE BANK ON MONDAY

BESSENT DISMISSES TREASURY MARKET CONCERNS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the bond market remains in “very good shape” despite 10-year yields reaching their highest since 2023. He also downplayed Thursday’s smaller-than-expected buyback, saying Treasury purchased $5.19 billion versus a $6 billion maximum because bondholders were reluctant to sell long-term securities.
TRUMP: MAYBE I DON'T GO FULL INTO IRAN BECAUSE OF ELECTION

U.S. DIESEL BREAKS $6 FOR FIRST TIME EVER The U.S. average diesel price surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time, according to GasBuddy, up nearly 60% since the Iran war began. Supply remains extremely tight, with U.S. diesel inventories 13% below their five-year average, while Brent surged to $107.63. Record fuel costs risk reigniting inflation across U.S. supply chains ahead of the midterms.

APPLE’S $1,999 FOLDABLE FACES DEMAND TEST Apple’s new iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, but analysts question whether its appeal can extend beyond wealthy early adopters. Counterpoint still expects Apple to sell nearly 6 million units by year-end, potentially capturing 25% of the global foldable market on pent-up demand and brand strength alone.

TRUMP SUGGESTS ELECTION MAY LIMIT IRAN ESCALATION President Donald Trump said the upcoming election could influence whether the U.S. goes “fully” into Iran, while insisting he has no regrets over the conflict. Trump also claimed the U.S. controls the Strait of Hormuz and said American forces took out 22 boats there overnight.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN WAR TO END AFTER MIDTERMS President Donald Trump reiterated that he expects the war with Iran to end “right after” the midterm elections, saying Tehran is “in deep trouble.” Trump also claimed Iran’s missile stockpile has been largely wiped out, while acknowledging the country will retain some missile capability.

TRUMP DISMISSES AI EXTINCTION FEARS President Donald Trump says he has “no” concerns that AI could lead to human extinction, arguing the priority is ensuring the U.S. maintains its technological lead over China. Trump estimates America is roughly one year ahead of China in AI, warning that losing that advantage would put the U.S. in a “very bad position.”

TRUMP REPORTEDLY REJECTS MBS REQUEST TO STRIKE HOUTHIS Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman asked President Trump to launch airstrikes against the Houthis, according to Axios, citing U.S. officials. Trump reportedly refused, as Washington seeks to avoid direct involvement, even as the Houthis expand near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

IRAN, PAKISTAN DISCUSS PATH BACK TO TALKS Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir discussed efforts to de-escalate the U.S.-Iran conflict, a Pakistani security official told Reuters. The talks also covered a potential return to diplomacy and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, as regional tensions continue to escalate.

FRANCE DEBT CANCELLATION PLAN SLAMMED AS “DANGEROUS” Bank of France chief Emmanuel Moulin warned that Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to cancel 18% of France’s national debt would amount to a default, calling it “illegal, dangerous and useless.” Moulin warned the plan could fuel inflation and drive interest rates higher, echoing criticism from ECB President Christine Lagarde.

U.S. DIESEL SURGES ABOVE $6, INFLATION RISK BUILDS U.S. diesel prices hit a record $6.06 a gallon, with California approaching $8, as global supply disruptions tighten the market. With diesel crucial to shipping, agriculture and construction, higher costs risk feeding directly into consumer inflation just as seasonal demand rises. Continued disruption around Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb could keep prices elevated for longer.

GULF STATES WEIGH TALKS WITH IRAN OVER HORMUZ Gulf states are considering rare talks with Iran next week over the future of the Strait of Hormuz, with Oman seeking a meeting of GCC and Iranian foreign ministers. The talks could focus on restoring maritime traffic through the critical energy chokepoint, though escalating Houthi tensions may complicate plans and the meeting remains unconfirmed.

Bloomberg Economics argues the shift is structural: rising government debt, weaker global savings, higher defense spending and the AI investment boom are pushing borrowing costs higher. TRADERS NOW SEE ABOUT A 90% CHANCE OF A FED RATE HIKE NEXT WEEK, VS ABOUT 70% BEFORE THE INFLATION REPORT

US INFLATION ACCELERATES — FED HIKE RISK RISES US inflation picked up in August, strengthening the case for another Fed rate hike next week. Headline CPI rose 0.4% M/M and 3.4% Y/Y, while core CPI increased 0.3% M/M. Gasoline was a key driver, with oil back above $100/barrel adding to inflation concerns. Markets had been pricing roughly a 70% chance of a 25bp hike ahead of the report. Higher inflation + resilient employment + elevated oil prices = increasing pressure on the Fed to tighten.

US CPI: Inflation Comes In Hotter Than Expected August US inflation data delivered a firmer-than-expected headline reading, adding another complication to the Federal Reserve outlook. Headline CPI rose 0.396% M/M on an unrounded basis, effectively 0.4%, compared with expectations of around 0.39%. The bigger surprise came from core CPI, which increased 0.290% M/M, versus expectations of around 0.22% and up from 0.215% in the previous month. US CORE INFLATION UPSIDE DRIVEN BY SUPERCORE The latest inflation details show the upside surprise was driven by supercore services, while core goods were softer than expected. Lodging was a notable upside outlier, while housing came in softer. Medical services and airfares were relatively benign in CPI, although related PPI components had already surprised higher. The composition suggests underlying services inflation remains a key challenge for the Fed.

US DATA: RECORD CELL PHONE PRICE JUMP BOOSTS CORE CPI August inflation data carried a hawkish signal as wireless phone service prices surged 5.9% — the largest increase on record. The jump alone added around 0.08 percentage points to core CPI and will also feed into core PCE. Housing inflation was softer than expected, but its lower weighting in PCE means the underlying picture could still keep pressure on the Fed.

IRAN CONFIRMS REGIONAL TALKS ON HORMUZ SHIPPING Iran’s Foreign Ministry confirmed a regional meeting will be held in Oman on Monday, involving Iran, Iraq and other Gulf states to discuss security and commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran says the meeting will review Iran-Oman plans for temporary safe shipping routes, while warning that Hormuz security cannot be guaranteed as long as what it describes as U.S. military and economic pressure continues.
SITUATIONAL AWARENESS ACTIVE IN OPTIONS MARKET: CNBC CITING SOURCES

S&P 500’S 8,000 MILESTONE REMAINS ELUSIVE The S&P 500 is still 5.4% away from 8,000, as rising bond yields, sticky inflation and a hawkish Fed outlook stall the rally. CFRA still targets 8,050 by year-end, but warns a 5%-10% correction would not be unusual. Despite the macro risks, Wall Street remains relatively calm, with the VIX below 20 and corporate earnings providing support.

HASSETT SAYS INFLATION IS “CLEARLY DECELERATING” White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett says inflation has clearly slowed over the past three months, while stressing that the Fed’s independence should be respected. Hassett added that Trump will likely have an opinion if the Fed hikes rates, and said proposed $5,000 Trump payments could be delivered in a fiscally responsible way, potentially through reconciliation.

TRUMP VOWS $5,000 “DIVIDEND” FOR U.S. ADULTS President Donald Trump says his proposed $5,000 payment to U.S. adults “will happen,” arguing Americans deserve to benefit from what he described as trillions of dollars in economic development and investment. Trump did not provide new details on timing or funding in the statement, but insisted he intends to deliver the payments.
